selectedOriginals.caption: This photo shows Penarth Pier and Pavilion after its refurbishment in 2012.
selectedOriginals.inspection: 2014 restored original individually inspected: white tapering corner towers with diamond grilles and silver fish-scale domes/finials, zinc barrel roof/four tall side dormers, dark multipane windows, white/green traceried railings, broad concrete pavilion support frame and slender braced iron neck, two cream timber shelters and head hut. Temporary site fence not included.

sources.inspection: Primary designation read: about200m pier,15m historic landing-stage width, cast-iron original center and concrete landward/landing ends; two boarded shelters/head ticket office. Main1929 concrete pavilion: four tapering corner towers with pinnacled Moghul roofs/deep bracketed eaves, large diaper grilles/two smaller paired tiers, convex landward lobby/concave classical shop wings, curved seaward glazed colonnade,11-bay barrel roof/four tall side windows/ridge ventilators. Legacy parenthetical seaward(W) is a compass typo; actual mapped/aerial seaward direction ESE is used.
sources.scopeCorrection: Do not reconstruct lost1931 wooden concert hall; surviving shore pavilion predates fire.

sources.inspection: Restoration architect Purcell project statement read:2013 conservation retained/repaired ferro-concrete and added shiny fish-scale metal roof coverings; ends/internal spaces altered for cafe/observatory/cinema. Two external photographs individually inspected as credited; no photograph pixels embedded.
Current operator read:1929 pavilion, vaulted main gallery and current cultural venue. Supports surviving named structure, not physical survey.

Operator2023 maintenance read: replacement of lower deck/upper balcony boards in keeping with main pier plus new lighting. Geometry remains selected restored form; temporary lighting/closures not claimed.

Aerial individually inspected: ESE pier, white four-dome pavilion with long zinc roof/ridge/four south dormers, convex seaward terraces, low curving shore shop wings, paired middeck shelters, broad open head/ticket hut and narrow lower landing edge. Own outline distinct from promenade/baths/apartments.

scope: Restored four-domed white shore pavilion, zinc barrel roof, curved glazed colonnade/terraces and shop wings; timber pier on iron/concrete supports, two shelters, head hut and landing.
limitations: Selected post2013 restored exterior from local2013/2014 originals,2017 full-pier/2024 head context and primary architect/Cadw/operator evidence. Original hand-authored roof profiles, zinc scale seams, lattice/rail motifs, hidden walls/windows, heights and support spacings remain proportional estimates, not survey/scans.

Independent mapped main pavilion body about35x17m with shore wings spanning46m; own deck extends about183m from street-side pavilion front to head, with full shore-wing/pier envelope193m. Primary about200m agrees broadly. Current mapped broad head widthabout28m differs from legacy15m landing-stage description; preserve actual mapped head and record historical/generalized-width ambiguity.

Independent terrain remains unchanged. Marine/coastal returns do not establish seabed, tide, actual landing level or pile embedment. Fixed supports/landing poses are bounded visual estimates; geographic activation requires current contact review; footprint replacement disabled.

No lost1931 seaward theatre reconstructed. Neighboring promenade/baths/apartments, separate K6 kiosk, beach/water/boats, temporary flags/string lights/signs/people and loose furnishings/interiors excluded. Integral structural railings/clock/lamps retained approximately; no source pixels redistributed.
